name: TRIZ (Creative Destruction)
deliverable: Systematic cessation of self-sabotaging behaviors and counter-productive habits

steps.text: Invert the goal: ask the room to design the worst possible version of the system, one that guarantees the failure they fear.
Have people draft in silence for two minutes, then build one ruinous list per table for eight minutes.
Audit each item honestly: ask whether the team already does this, even slightly, and mark every yes.
Pick the marked habit doing the most damage and name the first concrete thing to stop.
Assign an owner and a date to each cessation; do not replace it with a new improvement project.

failure: The audit avoids circling familiar bad habits to protect people's feelings, so the room generates a list that describes someone else's organization.
intervention: Circle an obvious item yourself and say: "We cannot remove what we will not name. What else here are we pretending we do not do?"
provenance: Source protocol: the steps follow the written script in the source.

origin.note: TRIZ originates with Genrich Altshuller; this creative-destruction version is the Liberating Structures adaptation.
